nav.priceTip: Fixed sandbox price: $100,000 per BTC, so $100 = 100,000 sats. The real price moves all the time.

assets.createdRandom: Your wallet was just drawn at random: 12 words picked from a list. Randomness is what protects you — nobody can guess your combination, not even the person who wrote the software.
assets.createdWords: These 12 words are the wallet. Every address comes from them, so whoever holds the words holds the money. There is no extra password to remember: the words are the key.
assets.createdRealLife: In real life: write them on paper, offline, and never in an email, a photo or a message. If you lose your device, those words are the only way to get your money back.
assets.createdWhere: You can show them later in the wallet's Backup section.
assets.receiveHint: Reusing an address works, but a fresh address per payment keeps people from linking all your transactions together.
assets.addressesHint: The wallet balance is the sum of its addresses. Each address keeps whatever it received.
assets.seedWarning: These 12 words give access to every sat in this wallet. Nobody should ever ask for them: not a support agent, not a website, not a friend.
assets.publicTip: Sandbox public address (lc1q), derived from your 12 words. Safe to share. This is not a real Bitcoin address.
assets.secretTip: 12 sandbox words. Never share them. This is not a real BIP39 seed.

services.title: Services
services.buySubtitle: Sandbox exchange service: it turns your $ into sats and sends them to your address.
services.destinationHint: The exchange sends the sats to this address. That is all it needs to pay you.
services.kycNote: In real life an exchange would also ask for an ID document (KYC) to open an account. It never asks for your 12 words: an address is enough to receive.
